name: Revenge of Gann
summary: At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for his fallen tribe.

sections.title: A Symbol of Domination
sections.body: Bael Modan’s dwarven excavation covers ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors depend on a gyrocopter for reach and military strength. It waits on a watchtower above the dig, surveying the Barrens and guarding the dwarves’ supply lines. To Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

sections.title: Turned Upon Its Makers
sections.body: After recovering Prospector Khazgorm’s plans, Gann Stonespire makes a specialized charge called the Explosive Stick of Gann. He plants it on the flying machine and turns the dwarves’ invention against them. The blast destroys a vital military asset and humiliates the Bael'dun contingent. It also honors the spirits of Gann’s lost tribe.

faq.q: Why does Gann want to destroy the flying machine specifically?
faq.answer: The flying machine supports Bael Modan’s infrastructure and gives the dwarves aerial reconnaissance. To Gann, it embodies dwarven power and looms over land his slaughtered tribe once called home.

faq.q: Where is the flying machine located at Bael Modan?
faq.answer: The flying machine sits on a wooden tower platform halfway down the ramp into the main excavation pit, apart from the primary dwarven fortress.

faq.q: How did Gann create the explosive device?
faq.answer: Gann made the Explosive Stick of Gann from technical schematics and engineering plans recovered from Prospector Khazgorm. He turned the dwarves’ own designs against them.

faq.q: What tribe does Gann belong to?
faq.answer: Gann belongs to the Stonespire tribe, a tauren clan that once lived in the southern Barrens. The Ironforge dwarven excavation drove them out by force and destroyed their settlement.

faq.q: Does destroying the machine stop the excavation permanently?
faq.answer: Destroying the machine cripples Bael Modan’s air strength and infrastructure, and gives Gann personal revenge. The heavily entrenched dwarven diggers and fortress remain an active Alliance stronghold in the region.

faq.q: What recognition does Gann offer upon finishing this mission?
faq.answer: Gann says the hero who destroyed the machine will be revered in Thunder Bluff as a defender of sacred tauren lands and a lasting champion of his lost tribe.

angles.text: For a tauren, destroying dwarven war machines to avenge the Stonespire clan echoes the defense of ancestral ground from desecration.
For the Horde, crippling Bael Modan’s flying machine weakens an Alliance weapon that can scout and strike deep into the southern Barrens.
For an engineer, the explosive turns Ironforge blueprints against a gyrocopter in a clever act of field sabotage.
